held.title: Local `nativeThreadId` still holds the expired checkpoint's thread ID after it is dropped
held.body:
`let nativeThreadId = this.record.nativeThreadId` (line 1004) is read before `prepare` runs. When `prepare` finds the checkpoint missing, `dropExpiredCheckpoint()` clears `nativeThreadId` in the record, but the local variable keeps the old ID until `onThread` replaces it.

If the turn fails or is stopped after `prepare` but before `onThread` (for example, the clone in `addCourseFiles` fails or the runner never connects), any later code that writes this variable back to the record puts the dead thread ID back. That record would then pair `checkpoint: null` with a thread that exists in no sandbox, and the next turn would try to resume a thread that is gone instead of starting a new one. I could not see the code after this hunk that uses the variable, so I could not confirm this path.

Fix: set `nativeThreadId = null` next to the `dropExpiredCheckpoint()` call.
